### Part 167 (done): the recipe repo-sync mechanism (ADR-0121) had never actually been configured on 192.168.15.95 -- two real gaps found and fixed

`GET /v1/pkg/repo-config` returned an entirely empty `repo_url` -- despite shipping code-complete, this box had never actually been pointed at the project's own git remote. Configuring it surfaced a second real gap: `POST /pkg/sync` failed with `COULDNT_RESOLVE_HOST` despite 3 configured nameservers -- one (`.254`) doesn't run DNS at all, and the real internal resolver for `.home.arpa` (`192.168.15.200`) was never in the list. Both fixed; a real sync now pulls recipes directly from git (`added: 56` on first run). Every future recipe change on this box goes through `git commit` + `pkg sync` now, not ad-hoc `pkg recipe add`.

### Part 166 (done): glauth's "listener mystery" resolved a third time -- a real TOML authoring bug, not the ADR-0113 inotify gap it resembled

A fresh LDAP account rendered correctly into `glauth.cfg` but every bind failed with `User not found` -- no `could not start config-watcher` error this time (ADR-0113's original ENOSYS signature), and a genuine restart didn't help either. Root cause: `watchconfig = true` was placed after `[behaviors]` in the base config, so TOML parsed it as `behaviors.watchconfig`, not the top-level key glauth actually checks -- it never even attempted to start a watcher. Fixed by moving the key above any `[section]` header; verified via a real `ldapsearch` bind (`result: 0 Success`) against both `ldap-1` and `ldap-2`.

### Part 165 (done -- kernel rebuild deferred): root-caused the ADR-0165 production regression (ADR-0166)

Every ordinary `pkg install` against 192.168.15.95 failed 100% of the time once ADR-0165's real `memory_max`/`cpu_max` limits went live -- three redeploy-and-retry cycles were needed to get a real diagnostic out of a box with no shell: `perror()` calls reached nowhere (nothing mirrors stderr into the log store, the reverse is true), then a second round of the same mistake, then moving the actual logging to `main.c`'s own log-store-linked call site plus a precise `container_create_last_error_step()` finally surfaced it: `cgroup_create: write cpu.max: No such file or directory`. Root cause, confirmed against real kernel source: `CONFIG_CFS_BANDWIDTH` -- a distinct symbol from `CONFIG_CGROUP_SCHED`/`CONFIG_FAIR_GROUP_SCHED` (both already enabled), `default n`, never previously exercised. Kernel config fixed and committed; the actual kernel rebuild is deferred, blocked on a separate, real TCC-vs-binutils compiler issue not chased further this session. **Limits stay disabled on 192.168.15.95** until a kernel carrying the fix is deployed there.

### Part 163 (done): container resource limits (`memory_max`/`cpu_max`/`pids_max`) surfaced back, closing a write-only API gap (ADR-0165 follow-up)

Reported directly: "how do I see the number of allocated cpus and the number of allocated memory per container? I clicked on pkgbuild-0 and -1 and I cannot tell." `POST /containers` had accepted `memory_max`/`cpu_max`/`pids_max` since Phase 12, and ADR-0165 (Part 162) had just started setting them on every `__pkgbuild-N` sandbox -- but `registry_write_json_one()`, the one shared serializer behind both `GET /containers` and `GET /containers/{name}`, never included any of the three. A limit could be set and enforced with no way to ever see it again.

`registry_write_json_one()` now reads all three live from the real cgroup via `entry->handle.cgroup_fd` (a new `cgroup_read_cpu_max()` alongside the existing `cgroup_read_single_value()`), reflecting what's actually enforced right now rather than mirroring what was requested at creation -- confirmed correct for a running container and for one that has since exited but stays registered. `null` means unlimited, matching ADR-0165's own convention. `cixctl inspect`/`container list` gained matching columns; the web dashboard's container detail Summary tab gained "Memory limit"/"CPU limit"/"Process limit" fields, CPU rendered as a computed percentage-of-one-core (e.g. "50% (50000 100000)") alongside the raw cgroup pair.

Verified live end to end: a container created with explicit limits reported the exact values back through the API even after exiting; one created with none reported `null`/"unlimited" throughout. Confirmed through the real web UI via headless Chromium (`puppeteer-core`) for both cases.

### Part 162 (done): real cgroup memory/CPU limits on the pkgbuild sandbox (ADR-0165)

A burst of ~19 concurrent `pkg install` calls (rebuilding images for 192.168.15.95's 7 restored containers) left `cixd` completely unresponsive -- TCP still accepted connections, but no HTTP request ever completed again. Matches a previously-documented incident on this same box (ROADMAP Part 144), triggered the same way. Investigating the actual code found the real gap: every `__pkgbuild-N` build sandbox already goes through the identical `container_create()`/`struct cgroup_limits` mechanism a regular container uses, but `pkg.c`'s own build-spec construction only ever set `cg.name` -- `memory_max`/`cpu_max` were always left at "no limit." `max_concurrent_jobs` only ever capped how many builds run *at once*, never what any single one could consume.

Checking Proxmox during the incident showed flat ~6GB memory and idle CPU the whole time it was unresponsive -- not the rising-memory, sustained-CPU signature classic OOM/thrashing would show, so this doesn't cleanly confirm Part 144's own (already-hedged) "memory pressure" hypothesis either. The exact blocking mechanism remains unconfirmed both times. The resource-ceiling gap is real and worth closing regardless of the precise mechanism, though: a genuine deadlock is, if anything, more likely under concurrent load, not less.

Extends the existing `pkg-build-config` resource with `memory_max` (bytes, default 2GiB) and `cpu_max` (raw cgroup v2 `cpu.max` syntax, default `"100000 100000"` -- one full CPU), applied to every future build's own sandbox container. `PUT` is now a genuine partial update (only the fields given change), matching daemon-config/hostauth-config's own convention, rather than requiring `max_concurrent_jobs` on every call. `0`/`null` means unlimited, a deliberate opt-out.

Verified live: `__pkgbuild-0`'s real cgroup files (`memory.max`, `cpu.max`) confirmed to reflect the configured values during an actual running build, and that build completed successfully under the new default limits.

### Part 161 (done): installer ISO no longer boots blind

`mkinstalleriso`'s generated `grub.cfg` never set `gfxpayload`, so GRUB always attempted to negotiate a graphical video mode for the kernel handoff even though both menu entries only ever use plain text consoles -- confirmed live on a real Proxmox VM: "error: no suitable video mode found, Booting in blind mode" on every boot. Fixed with `set gfxpayload=text`. Verified via two real QEMU boots of a freshly built ISO: confirmed inherent to a genuinely video-device-less test harness either way, and confirmed gone with a real video device present where it previously always appeared.

### Part 160 (done): CLI prompt shows host.site.tld + real auth state, plus a real mid-session login/logout bug (ADR-0164)

`cixctl`'s interactive shell prompt now shows the connected daemon's full site FQDN (`instance.site.domain`, matching `siteconfig_host_fqdn()`) instead of just the bare instance name, and a trailing `>`/`#` for auth state -- the same convention real shells and network-device CLIs already use. Backed by a new `GET /whoami`, deliberately built on a new, non-mutating `hostauth_peek_token()` rather than the existing `hostauth_check_token()` -- the latter consumes a single-use (`idle_timeout_seconds: 0`) token just by checking it, which would have silently invalidated a session the moment the prompt refreshed.

Verifying the `#` transition surfaced a real, previously-invisible bug: `cmd_login()` persisted the new token to `~/.cixctl_token` for the *next* `cixctl` invocation, but never updated the *current* process's own in-memory client -- every command for the rest of that interactive session, mid-session, silently kept using the old (often empty) token despite "Logged in as X" printing successfully. `cmd_logout()` had the mirror gap. Both now update the live client's token too.

Also: 5 real commands (`kmod`, `kmod-build`, `kmod-config`, `sysctl`, `hostauth-sessions`) were fully dispatchable and documented in `--help`, but missing from the interactive shell's own separate Tab-completion list -- found by diffing `dispatch_command()`'s own recognized commands against that list programmatically, not by eye.

Verified: a real login/logout cycle against a live daemon (LDAP user + group created for the test) through a real pty, confirming the exact `>` -> `#` -> `>` transition text, not just the underlying JSON. Full regression sweep (`test_cli`, `test_hostauth`, `test_daemon`) -- zero failures.

### Part 159 (done): a malformed persisted state file must never be fatal to boot (ADR-0163)

Confirmed live on 192.168.15.95 during the Phase 5 rebrand migration: a `POST /system/restore` wrote an empty string as the literal content of `site_config.json` (the backup bundle's own `site_config` field was legitimately empty, and `do_system_restore()`'s own field validator deliberately treats an empty string as valid -- correct for most fields, wrong for this one). The next boot's `siteconfig_load()` failed to parse it, logged "malformed persisted site config," and returned -1 -- and since `cixd` is real PID 1 on an installed system, `main()`'s existing "any subsystem init failure is fatal" boot sequence turned that one bad file into `Kernel panic - not syncing: Attempted to kill init!`, unrecoverable short of a full reinstall (confirmed: a plain reset reproduced the identical panic, since the bad file was still on disk).

Fixed at two layers: `siteconfig_load()` itself now falls back to real, already-applied defaults on malformed/invalid content instead of returning an error; and new `boot_subsystem_init()` in `daemon/src/main.c` gates every one of the ~20 persisted-JSON-state `_init()` calls in the real `--init-mode` boot sequence -- a nonzero return there is now logged as a warning and treated as success (that subsystem keeps its defaults), while a plain/test invocation (not real PID 1, an ordinary process exit is harmless there) keeps the original fail-fast behavior unchanged. Deliberately not applied to the handful of boot steps with real mount/network side effects (`bootstrap_management_network()`, the `resolve_*_storage_placement()` family, `ensure_dir()`) -- a different, more consequential failure mode than "one JSON file didn't parse," left for its own dedicated review.

Verified: a real repro (an empty `site_config.json` written directly, then a plain daemon start) now logs the warning and boots successfully with defaults, where it previously would have been fatal. Full regression sweep (`test_daemon`, `test_system_backup`, `test_networks`, `test_daemon_net`) -- zero failures, confirming the non-init-mode fail-fast path is byte-for-byte unchanged.

### Part 158 (done): full project rename (ADR-0162, tasks #885-889)

The project is renamed for the first time, from the name it launched under to the one it carried until the Cix rebrand (Part 204). Full reasoning and consequences: ADR-0162. Every entry above this one in this file, and every entry in `docs/roadmap/ROADMAP.md`, was written under a previous name and describes events that genuinely happened under it -- mechanically renamed to `Cix`/`cixd`/`cixctl` for reading consistency (this project's own docs treat every one of its names as the same continuously-developed system, not separate projects), not to rewrite what actually happened at the time. This entry is the marker for when and why.

Five sequenced phases (tracked as tasks #885-889), each committed and pushed separately:

1. **Brand assets** (`brand/`) -- logo mark, lockup variants, brand guidelines corrected against the real codebase (an AI-generated first draft had real errors: a nonexistent `/v1/hardware` endpoint, a false absolute "no eBPF" claim, a mark description that didn't match what was actually built).
2. **Code-level rename** -- `cixd`->`cixd`, `cixctl`->`cixctl`, `cix-install`/`-recover`->`cix-install`/`-recover`, `/var/lib/cix`->`/var/lib/cix`, default instance name/FQDN `cix`/`cix.internal`->`cix`/`cix.internal`, every code identifier and test fixture, the web dashboard (plus its own new favicon/header mark, surfacing and fixing a real, previously-latent gap: the static file server had no `.svg` MIME type case at all). A **newly generated** Secure Boot signing key, not a bytes-preserving rename -- CN `Cix Secure Boot Signing Key` -- accepted knowingly: any already-MOK-enrolled real hardware needs re-enrollment. 150 files, a perfectly symmetric 1805/1805-line diff (pure substitution, zero content drift), full clean rebuild and full regression sweep both clean.
3. **Current-state docs** -- README (a real prose rewrite of the intro and naming section, not blind substitution), API docs, all 13 guides, the architecture diagram, CLAUDE.md. `docs/mission/MISSION.md` deliberately left untouched -- frozen by its own rule, a proposed new charter drafted separately for the user's own explicit review rather than applied here.
4. **Historical docs** (this file, `docs/roadmap/ROADMAP.md`, all 128 ADR bodies) -- mechanically renamed, this entry (and ADR-0162) the marker for the event itself.
5. **Live deployment** (192.168.15.95) -- migrates via a full reinstall from a freshly built Cix installer ISO, not an in-place binary/data-directory migration: the user's own explicit choice mid-rebrand, to genuinely exercise the real install path (kernel module + sysctl management, both added since the box's own last full install) rather than just patching a running system. `POST /system/backup`'s existing config-only bundle carries container/network/DNS/site config across the reinstall; PKI/LDAP data outside that bundle's scope (ADR-0033's own established boundary) is re-provisioned fresh afterward, the same real sequence this box has already been through once before.

Verified: full clean rebuild (`-Wall -Werror`), zero warnings, across every build target. Full daemon-linked regression sweep, run individually with an orphan check after each -- zero regressions (one confirmed pre-existing flake and one confirmed environmental-contention false-failure, both unrelated, both already documented in `CLAUDE.md`). `docs/api/openapi.yaml` still parses as valid YAML; `docs/architecture/architecture.svg` still renders; every rebuilt SVG verified by real `rsvg-convert` render.

### Part 157 (done): parallel package builds -- Phase 4 implementation, concurrent-vs-serial byte-identical merge-back proof (ADR-0157, task #878) -- ADR-0157 fully closed

Phase 4 -- the last of ADR-0157's four phases (task #841 is now complete) -- and the decisive proof this design called for from its own first draft: not just that N genuinely different packages can install concurrently (Phase 2's own test already proved that for N=2), but that the daemon's single, shared `g_pkgbuild_rootfs` merge-back sandbox produces byte-identical final content whether N installs run concurrently or strictly serially.

New `test/test_pkg_concurrent_stress.c`: two entirely separate `cixd` instances (own `--data-dir`, own `--port`, own fresh bootstrap) install the identical set of 3 packages -- one daemon concurrently (no wait between the three `POST`s, `pkg-build-config` pinned to `max_concurrent_jobs=3` for a deterministic boundary, plus a 4th attempt correctly rejected `409` while all 3 slots are busy), the other strictly serially (one at a time, waiting for each to reach `installed`). The comparison: both runs converge on the identical image-version hash (ADR-0108's version directory name is an order-independent hash of the sorted manifest), and -- the real proof -- `diff -rq` between the two runs' base image rootfs trees reports zero content differences. Confirmed deterministic across three consecutive runs, not a one-off pass.

A real, non-bug finding along the way, recorded rather than silently worked around: the first unfiltered diff reported six differences, all under `/dev` -- `pkg_seed_image_baseline()`'s (ADR-0150) fixed baseline device nodes, which `diff` cannot meaningfully compare as "content" at all (it flags a character-special file as an unresolvable difference regardless of whether both sides genuinely match). Fixed with a documented, narrow `--exclude=dev` -- out of scope for what this test actually proves, not a weakening of the real comparison.

`test/test_pkg.c`'s own `hbtest` hostbuild poll timeout (30 attempts, 9s -- tuned back when it was the only build in flight) raised to 100 attempts (30s): ADR-0157 Phase 2 made that same poll window genuinely share the box with a second, real concurrent gcc build (`hbconcurrent`), so the old single-build-tuned window is now marginal under real CPU contention -- confirmed as timing, not logic, since the daemon always reached `installed` eventually, just occasionally past the old window. A separate, second class of flake investigated and ruled out entirely: a `cixd` orphaned by an earlier, harness-killed test run had kept holding `test_pkg`'s own port, so several subsequent runs were silently talking to a stale daemon from a *different* test's data directory -- every one of the resulting failures (different assertions failing on different reruns, a daemon that wouldn't exit cleanly on `SIGTERM`) stopped completely the instant that orphaned process was killed, confirming this was never a defect in the code under test.

Verified: `test_pkg_concurrent_stress.c` compiles `-Wall -Werror` clean; full clean rebuild across every build target, zero warnings. Full daemon-linked regression sweep, run individually with an orphan check after each -- zero regressions, zero leaked `cixd` processes. ADR-0157's own status and a new "Phase 4 implementation" section, `docs/adr/README.md`'s index row, and `docs/roadmap/ROADMAP.md` updated to reflect all four phases shipped and this ADR fully closed.

### Part 156 (done): parallel package builds -- Phase 3 implementation, real ceiling raised to 10, config surface + CLI/web/docs (ADR-0157, task #877)

Phase 3 of ADR-0157's phased design (Phase 2 -- concurrency limit 1->2 plus its real prerequisites -- shipped as Part 155 immediately prior). `PKG_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS` raised from Phase 2's placeholder 2 to the task's own real target, 10, plus the operator-configurable ceiling and full CLI/web/docs coverage the design always scoped for this phase.

`GET`/`PUT /v1/system/pkg-build-config` (`{"max_concurrent_jobs": N}`, range `[1, 10]`) mirrors `pkg-cache-config`'s own shape exactly (ADR-0122/ADR-0124 precedent) -- persisted, repointed alongside the cache/artifact configs on a rebuildable-storage migration. `chain_alloc()` now bounds its search by the configured ceiling instead of the raw compile-time array size -- lowering it takes effect for the *next* chain-allocation only, never disrupting chains already running in already-claimed slots.

New `cixctl pkg-build-config show|set --max-concurrent-jobs=N` (a top-level command, matching the REST path being under `/v1/system/`) and a new "Package Builds" web dashboard page under the existing Host nav group, both mirroring `rolling-config`'s own established shape.

`docs/api/openapi.yaml` + `docs/api/README.md` updated together (new `PkgBuildConfig` schema/path, summary table row, a new Package Manager narrative paragraph, and three now-stale "v1 serializes installs"/"only one job at a time" claims elsewhere in that doc corrected to describe the real, now-configurable ceiling); `docs/guides/cli-reference.md` gained the two new command rows; ADR-0157's own status and a new "Phase 3 implementation" section, and `docs/adr/README.md`'s index row, updated to match.

The pre-existing Phase 2 concurrency-boundary tests in `test/test_pkg.c` (written against Phase 2's placeholder default of 2) needed one deliberate adjustment, not a redesign: the test now explicitly sets the ceiling to 2 right after the daemon starts, so those assertions stay meaningful without needing 11 concurrent packages to exercise a now-10-wide default. New Phase 3 coverage proves the real default is 10, `0`/`11` are both rejected `400`, and -- the direct, load-bearing proof -- lowering the ceiling to 1 makes a second concurrent install genuinely get `409` again, not just that the number is echoed back correctly.

Verified: full clean rebuild (`-Wall -Werror`) across daemon/CLI, zero warnings; `web/app.js` passes `node --check`; `openapi.yaml` parses as valid YAML. Full daemon-linked regression sweep (run individually after batched runs showed unrelated environmental cross-test contention, confirmed by clean reruns in isolation) -- zero regressions from this change. One confirmed pre-existing, unrelated flake (`test_kmod_build`, a real kernel compile occasionally missing its own poll timeout) reproduces identically with this change fully reverted.

### Part 155 (done): parallel package builds -- Phase 2 implementation, concurrency limit raised 1->2 (ADR-0157, task #876)

Phase 2 of ADR-0157's phased design (Phase 1 shipped earlier as Part ~131): `PKG_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS` raised from 1 to 2, plus every real prerequisite the ADR's own "Correction found" paragraph identified once implementation actually started (moved to `pkg.h` since `main.c` needs it too, not left `pkg.c`-private).

**Per-build container identity**: `pkg_build_container_name(chain_idx, ...)` computes `"__pkgbuild-<chain_idx>"` (exported, replaces the single fixed `PKG_BUILD_CONTAINER_NAME` every build used to share -- `registry_create()` rejects a duplicate name outright, so two genuinely concurrent builds needed distinct real container names, not just distinct internal bookkeeping). The inverse, `pkg_build_container_chain_index()`, replaces two bare `strcmp()`s against the old fixed name (`handle_container_event()`, `handle_stop()`'s own `was_pkgbuild` special case) that would otherwise have silently stopped matching once the name carried a chain suffix.

**Fetch-side conn/entry threading**: `struct conn` gained `pkg_chain_idx`, threaded through `register_pkg_fetch_pidfd()`/`register_pkg_build_output()` and all 8 real call sites, and through `pkg_fetch_completed()`/`pkg_build_completed()`/`pkg_try_start_queued_rebuild()`/`pkg_build_spawn_failed()`/the four `pkg_build_output_*()` accessors on the `pkg.c` side.

**Chain-aware build-output/live-tail WebSocket**: `g_build_output_entry` (a single pointer) became `g_build_output_entries[PKG_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS]`; `g_build_log_ws_conns[]`'s own broadcast/teardown now take a `chain_idx` so a client watching one concurrent build never sees another's output or gets torn down when a *different* build finishes. `GET /v1/pkg/build/log` gained real `?name=&image=` query params (`pkg_chain_index_for_target()`) to pick which build to attach to, with a backward-compatible fallback (`pkg_active_chain_indices()`) for a caller supplying neither: exactly 1 active chain still attaches implicitly (every pre-Phase-2 client's existing behavior), more than 1 now asks for an explicit `?name=` (400) rather than guessing.

**`pkg_image_recipe_apply_start()`'s old shared-field busy-lock trick** (reusing a chain slot's own `name`/`image` fields as a bulk-artifact-fetch busy marker -- correct with exactly one slot, wrong once a free slot no longer means "nothing running") replaced with a dedicated `g_image_apply_busy`/`g_image_apply_image` pair and a `pkg_any_job_busy()` helper shared by all three "can a new top-level job start" gates.

**First real concurrency test** (`test/test_pkg.c`): two different packages installed back to back with no wait -- the second now gets `202`/`fetching` where it used to get `409` -- then a third attempt while both slots are occupied correctly gets `409`; both original installs verified to reach `installed` with working binaries. Repeated for the hostbuild/ordinary-install combination. One real race found and fixed while writing this (documented in ADR-0157's own "Phase 2 implementation" section): the first attempt at the second scenario reused a fixture with a deliberately-invalid checksum, whose failure was fast enough to free its chain slot before the third-job `409` check even ran -- replaced with a fixture that takes a genuine build to finish, removing the race rather than papering over it with a sleep.

`docs/adr/0157-parallel-package-builds-design.md`'s own Status and new "Phase 2 implementation" section, and `docs/adr/README.md`'s index row, updated to match. Phases 3-4 (config surface + real default of 10, N-way stress test + byte-identical merge-back proof) remain open.

Verified: `daemon/src/pkg.c`/`daemon/src/main.c` both compile `-Wall -Werror` clean; full daemon-linked regression sweep (`test_pkg`, `test_pkg_build_log`, `test_pkg_sync`, `test_pkg_cache`, `test_kmod_build`, `test_image_recipe`, `test_container_recipe`, `test_rolling_restart`, and every other daemon-linked test binary) passes with zero regressions.

### Part 154 (done): USB composite-device metadata + hotplug reaction -- all four phases implemented together (ADR-0161, task #884)

Full implementation of ADR-0161's phased design (Part 150), shipped as one combined deliverable per the ADR's own explicit "not incrementally" decision, not staged.

**Phase A** (composite-device interface metadata): `struct discovered_device` gains `interfaces[]`/`interface_count` (`daemon/include/device.h`); `enumerate_usb_one()` correlates each real per-interface sysfs entry (`<device>:1.<N>`, a sibling in the same flat `/sys/bus/usb/devices/` directory `usb_name_is_device()`'s own top-level walk already skips) back to its owning whole device. `GET /v1/devices` now reports `class`/`subclass`/`protocol`/`number` for every real interface a composite device exposes -- purely descriptive, the passthrough unit stays the whole device, confirmed live against a real 5-interface Bluetooth-class device in this sandbox.

**Phase B** (opt-in `optional: true` device grant): `POST /containers`' own `devices[]` array gains a per-entry object shape (`{"id":..., "optional": true}`) alongside the pre-existing bare-string form -- an unresolvable `optional: true` entry no longer fails creation; the container is created without that grant, and the raw reference is remembered in a new, live-run-only `registry_entry.pending_devices[]` (a restart-capable container's own persisted create-body already carries the reference for free via `containerdef.c`'s existing replay -- no new persistence mechanism needed for that case).

**Phase C** (`NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT` listener): `start_uevent_watch()`, modeled on `start_kmsg_watch()`'s own async epoll-registration shape (not `rtnetlink.c`'s synchronous one) -- a new `CONN_UEVENT` conn kind, best-effort like its kmsg sibling. Filters to `SUBSYSTEM=usb` and whole-device `DEVPATH`s only (the identical rule `usb_name_is_device()` already applies, inlined rather than exported for one line of logic). Deliberately treats the uevent purely as a trigger ("something USB just changed, go recheck"), not as a source of device identity -- real hardware doesn't populate uevent payload fields identically across every device class, and this daemon already has a robust, fresh way to discover exactly that (`device.c`'s own sysfs walk).

**Phase D** (live attach/detach): `POST`/`DELETE /v1/containers/{name}/devices` -- the same two-layer shape ADR-0156 already established for networks (a real, callable-by-hand primitive first; Phase C's hotplug reconciliation is just another caller of it). `registry_device_live_attach()`/`_live_detach()` (new, `registry.c`) rebuild the full `BPF_CGROUP_DEVICE` program from `registry_entry.devices[]` (extended with `type`/`major`/`minor`/`live`) and re-`ATTACH` against the container's already-open `cgroup_fd` -- an atomic replace, empirically verified safe in the ADR's own real probe (2,000,000 concurrent `open()` attempts spanning the swap, zero succeeded). mknod/unlink reach into the running container via `/proc/<pid>/root`, the identical host-side mechanism ADR-0153's live file write already established.

A real correctness edge case found and fixed beyond what the ADR's own text worked out in this much depth: a live detach down to **zero** remaining devices cannot reuse `container_dev_bpf_attach()`'s own existing `device_count == 0` shortcut (correct at container-creation time -- "nothing attached yet" -- but silently wrong here, since it would leave the old, now-stale program, still granting the just-removed device, attached indefinitely). Fixed with a new, explicit primitive, `container_dev_bpf_detach()` (`src/container_dev.c`, a real `BPF_PROG_DETACH` -- `CIX_BPF_PROG_DETACH` was already defined in `include/linux_compat.h` but never previously called anywhere), reverting the cgroup to the same "no explicit program, inherit ancestor policy" state creation-time's own zero-device case already has.

The operator-facing "refuse to detach a create-time grant" policy (409) was deliberately kept OUT of `registry_device_live_detach()` itself -- mirrors `registry_network_detach()`'s own actual shape exactly (no built-in restriction; the REST handler checks first) specifically so Phase C's own hotplug-driven unplug revocation, which must NOT be bound by that same operator-facing restriction, can reuse the identical function unmodified.

New `cixctl container device attach|detach NAME ID` and `run --optional-device=ID`. `test/test_device_hotplug.c` proves Phase A (real composite-device interfaces), Phase B (optional grant doesn't fail creation, pending_devices echoed, non-optional behavior unchanged), and Phase D (live attach shows `live: true`, duplicate rejected, live detach then 404, create-time grant refused with 409) end-to-end against real hardware this sandbox actually has -- adapting rather than hardcoding, the same posture `test_daemon_devices.c` already established. Phase C's own listener is proven only indirectly (real hotplug events can't be triggered in this sandbox, the same class of gap CLAUDE.md's own NTP/BPF-probe environment notes already document) -- it calls the exact same `live_attach_one_device()`/`registry_device_live_detach()` primitives the test exercises directly, and daemon startup with the listener active is itself proven not to crash or hang.

`docs/api/openapi.yaml` + `docs/api/README.md` updated together (new `/containers/{name}/devices` paths, `Device.interfaces`, `ContainerCreateRequest.devices`' new object shape, `Container.pending_devices`, `ContainerDeviceAttachment.live`); `docs/guides/cli-reference.md` and a new "Device hotplug" section in `docs/guides/administration.md` updated to match; ADR-0161's own status and `docs/adr/README.md`'s index row updated to reflect all four phases as implemented together.

Verified: full clean rebuild (`-Wall -Werror`), zero warnings, across every one of this project's 66+ build targets. Full regression sweep across every daemon-linked test binary (54 in this pass, including the new `test_device_hotplug.c`), zero failures.

### Part 153 (done): on-demand in-tree kernel module build -- Phase B implementation (ADR-0159, task #883)

`POST /v1/system/kmod-build`: an ordinary hostbuild against the "kernel" recipe itself (the exact existing `pkg_hostbuild_start()` mechanism `POST /pkg/hostbuild` already drives, unmodified), gaining only an optional `config_symbols` array -- each entry a bare `CONFIG_*` name, validated strictly (charset + `CONFIG_` prefix), space-joined and threaded through as the build container's own real `CIX_KMOD_EXTRA_SYMBOLS` environment variable. `pkg_hostbuild_start()` gained one new parameter for this (every existing caller passes `NULL`, zero behavior change); `pkg_fetch_completed()`'s `build_envp` construction grew a 4th, conditional entry.

`kernel.recipe`'s own `build.sh` reads that variable: when set, writes each symbol as a `<SYMBOL>=m` line into a second fragment file and passes both fragments to the same `merge_config.sh` invocation already there; when unset (every pre-existing caller, including a bare `pkg hostbuild kernel`), the exact prior sequence runs unchanged -- strictly additive, not a second code path. This is deliberately simpler than the first design draft's proposal (a new, permanently-kept, version-pinned kernel build tree for on-demand module builds) -- dropped per direct "keep the mechanics simple, no extra moving parts" feedback in favor of reusing the already-proven whole-kernel rebuild, which guarantees kernel/module ABI match by construction. Real, honestly-stated tradeoff accepted in exchange: rebuilds the whole kernel, needs the existing A/B cutover + reboot to take effect, never a live addition.

New `cixctl kmod-build --build-image=IMAGE [--version=VERSION] [--symbol=CONFIG_FOO ...] [--upgrade] [--wait]`, reusing `poll_hostbuild()`/`fmt_pkg_line()` completely unmodified. `test/test_kmod_build.c` proves the real mechanism end-to-end with a tiny fixture recipe (isolated to the test's own `--data-dir=` recipes directory, no collision with the real git-tracked `kernel.recipe`) whose `pkg_build()` writes the env var's own value straight to a file -- confirming `CIX_KMOD_EXTRA_SYMBOLS` genuinely reaches the real build container, not just that the job completes. A real bug was caught and fixed while writing this test: the first draft of the new REST handler freed its parsed JSON body before its own `build_image`/`version` string pointers (which point *into* that parsed tree) were actually used by `pkg_hostbuild_start()` -- a real use-after-free, caught by an unexpected `400` where a `404` was expected, not by any sanitizer (this project's `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=0`/TCC toolchain has none); fixed by copying both fields into local buffers before freeing the parsed body, the same "own your inputs before releasing what they point into" discipline this project's JSON-handling code already follows elsewhere.

`docs/api/openapi.yaml` + `docs/api/README.md` updated together (new `/system/kmod-build` path, reusing the existing `PkgEntry` schema); `docs/guides/cli-reference.md` and `docs/guides/kernel-build-and-ab-updates.md` updated with the new command and workflow; ADR-0159's own status and `docs/adr/README.md`'s index row updated to reflect Phase B as implemented (Phase C stays deliberately undesigned, exactly as the ADR's own recommendation scoped it).

Verified: full clean rebuild (`-Wall -Werror`), zero warnings, across every one of this project's 66+ build targets. Full regression sweep across every daemon-linked test binary, zero failures.

### Part 152 (done): kernel module management REST API -- Phase A implementation (ADR-0159, task #882)

Full implementation of ADR-0159 Phase A: two new daemon modules, `kmod.c` (real `modprobe`/`modinfo` fork+exec, mirroring `pki.c`'s own `run_openssl()` shape for stdout/stderr capture, plus a direct, fork-free `/proc/modules` reader) and `kmodconfig.c` (persisted per-module `default_options` + `autoload`, mirroring `sysctlconfig.c`'s own shape). New endpoints: `GET /v1/system/kmod` (live loaded-module list), `GET`/`POST`/`DELETE /v1/system/kmod/{name}` (modinfo / load / unload), `GET /v1/system/kmod-config` + `PUT`/`DELETE /v1/system/kmod-config/{name}` (persisted defaults). `modprobe -r`, not a bare `rmmod`, backs unload -- real, reverse-dependency-aware removal, per the ADR's own explicit decision.

A new `load_configured_modules()` boot step completes the four-step boot ordering ADR-0159/ADR-0160 jointly established: `load_boot_modules()` (ADR-0061's fixed hardware-detection list) -> `apply_configured_sysctls()` (ADR-0160) -> the management network -> `load_configured_modules()` (this one, deliberately last -- operator-configured autoload is the least boot-critical of the four). Best-effort per module at boot, matching `load_boot_modules()`'s own established "missing hardware is the expected case" posture.

Real `modinfo` output is parsed field-by-field (not a fixed-column assumption) into a JSON object -- `parm:` lines (`name:description (type)`) become a `params` array, `depends:` becomes a real array, `intree:` becomes a boolean -- any field a given module doesn't report is simply omitted rather than forced to a placeholder.

This project's own dev/build sandbox has no real `/usr/bin/modprobe`/`modinfo` staged at all (only a real installed image does, via `kmod.recipe` -- the identical, already-established gap `load_boot_modules()`'s own comment already documents for the pre-existing hardware-detection path). `test/test_kmod.c` proves everything provable here for real: `GET /v1/system/kmod` against real `/proc/modules` (cross-checked against a ground-truth read the test performs independently), full `kmod-config` CRUD including partial (read-modify-write) updates, and every error path -- plus confirms the load/unload/modinfo endpoints fail *cleanly* (a real `404`, never a crash) when the real binary is absent, the same class of sandbox gap CLAUDE.md's own NTP `clock_settime()` and BPF-probe bullets already document. Their actual success path needs verifying on a real installed box.

New `cixctl kmod ls|show|load|unload` and `kmod-config ls|set|rm` CLI commands. `docs/api/openapi.yaml` + `docs/api/README.md` updated together (new paths, `KmodEntry`/`KmodInfo`/`KmodParam`/`KmodConfigEntry` schemas, a narrative section matching the sysctl section's own shape); `docs/guides/cli-reference.md` and a new "Kernel modules" section in `docs/guides/administration.md` updated to match.

Verified: full clean rebuild (`-Wall -Werror`), zero warnings, 66+ build targets. Full regression sweep, zero failures.

### Part 151 (done): host-level sysctl REST API -- implementation (ADR-0160, task #881)

Full implementation of ADR-0160's design (Part 150 below): a new `sysctlconfig.c`/`.h` persisted-config module (mirroring `devicemap.c`'s established `X_init`/`X_repoint`/`save_state`/`load_state` shape), wired into `main.c` as `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /v1/system/sysctl/{key}` + `GET /v1/system/sysctl`, and a new `apply_configured_sysctls()` boot step ordered between `load_boot_modules()` and `bootstrap_management_network()`. Reuses `container_net_apply_sysctl()` (previously per-container-netns-only) unmodified for the live `/proc/sys` write, since the dots-to-slashes translation it already does is netns-agnostic. Sysctl value typing is generic by content (a plain JSON string for a single-token value, a JSON array for a multi-token one, e.g. `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range`) rather than a curated per-key schema, resolving the one open question the ADR left unresolved, by explicit user choice against the initial recommendation of plain verbatim strings. `PUT` persists by default (reapplied at every boot) with an explicit `"persist": false` opt-out; `DELETE` only ever removes a key from the persisted boot-apply list, never the live value.

New `cixctl sysctl show|get|set|rm` CLI commands. `test/test_sysctl.c` proves the full surface end-to-end against this sandbox's own real `/proc/sys` -- the one daemon-linked test in this project that can't use an isolated `mkdtemp` state dir for the thing it's actually testing (host kernel state is inherently shared), so every real write it performs is a deliberately idempotent no-op (`net.ipv4.ip_forward`'s and `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range`'s own already-current values, written straight back), verified unchanged before and after every run.

A real, previously-undocumented platform behavior surfaced while writing this test: this project's own HTTP request parser does not decode percent-escapes in request paths at all (`%2F` in a URL passes through as the literal three characters, never becomes `/`) -- a validation test targeting "a key containing a literal slash" has to send a real embedded `/` directly in the path, not a percent-encoded one, to actually reach the handler with a slash present.

### Part 150 (done): three new subsystem designs -- kernel modules, host sysctl, USB hotplug (ADR-0159/0160/0161, tasks #879/#880)

Design-only, per explicit request: gather every clarifying question/ambiguity first, then write ADRs, discuss and reflect -- no implementation until specifically requested. All three grounded in direct code reading (existing `device.c`/`devicemap.c`/`container_dev.c`, ADR-0061's already-shipped kernel-module build/staging work, the `pkg hostbuild` pattern, `start_kmsg_watch()`'s async-netlink-adjacent shape) rather than invented abstractions -- each ADR names the real prerequisite gaps found only by reading the actual call sites, not knowable from the original ask alone.

- **ADR-0159** (kernel modules): Phase A wraps real `modprobe`/`rmmod`/`/proc/modules` for REST load/unload/list, with per-load and persisted-default module options and a REST-managed boot autoload list. Phase B (an additional in-tree module) was simplified after an initial draft's more complex persistent-build-tree design, per direct "keep the mechanics simple" feedback -- reuses the already-proven whole-kernel `kernel.recipe` hostbuild + existing A/B cutover instead, guaranteeing kernel/module ABI match by construction rather than new bookkeeping. Genuine out-of-tree (third-party) module support is explicitly left undesigned until a real need shows up.
- **ADR-0160** (host-level sysctl): direct `/proc/sys` file I/O (no external tool, reusing the exact translation scheme the existing per-container `--sysctl=` already has), fully open passthrough (host-auth write-gating only, by explicit request), a persisted boot-apply list.
- **ADR-0161** (USB hotplug + composite-device metadata): explicitly phased A-D by risk, not presented as one flat decision. Found a real prerequisite gap while designing: container creation hard-fails today on any device reference that isn't currently present, so live-attach-on-hotplug needs a new opt-in `optional: true` device entry and an entirely new manual live attach/detach primitive (mirroring ADR-0156's network shape) before hotplug automation has anything to call. The one genuinely uncertain mechanic (live `BPF_F_REPLACE` cgroup-program update) is flagged as needing a real empirical kernel-behavior check before implementation, not documentation-based confidence -- the same discipline ADR-0008's struct-packing lesson already established.

### Part 149 (done): parallel package builds -- Phase 1 implementation (ADR-0157, task #841)

Phase 1 of ADR-0157's own phased plan: the pure-refactor migration of `pkg.c`'s ~240 references to bare module statics (`g_current_job_*`, `g_dep_queue_*`, `g_build_*`) onto `struct pkg_entry` and a new small `struct pkg_chain` table, with the effective concurrency limit still fixed at 1 -- zero user-visible behavior change, fully verified against the existing test suite. Also fixes two unrelated, real, previously-undiscovered test bugs found while verifying this change (confirmed via a clean-baseline comparison to rule out causation): `test_https_chain`/`test_tls_throttle` hardcoded `HTTPS_PORT=8443` for their own client-side probes but never explicitly configured the daemon under test to actually listen there, silently broken since task #860 changed the real default to 443.

#### Changed
- `pkg.c`'s build-transient fields (overlay paths, argv/envp, output-capture pipe+buffer, cache-hit flag) now live on `struct pkg_entry` instead of bare module statics.
- A new `struct pkg_chain g_chains[PKG_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS]` (`== 1` for Phase 1) replaces `g_current_job_name`/`_image`/`_is_hostbuild`/`_build_image`/`_target_version` and `g_dep_queue`/`_count`/`_pos`/`_is_upgrade`.
- A real design correction found only by reading every call site (not knowable from ADR-0157's own original Context): `g_current_job_name`/`_image` turn out to also be reused, unrelated to any `pkg_entry`, as `pkg_image_recipe_apply_start()`'s own cross-subsystem busy lock -- ruling out a `pkg_entry*`-based chain design in favor of the plain name/image strings that shipped, which needed zero changes to that other call site.

#### Fixed
- `test_https_chain.c`/`test_tls_throttle.c` now explicitly request `https_port=8443` in their own daemon-config `PUT` instead of depending on the daemon's own default -- the exact coupling that let the #860 port-default change silently break them undetected.

### Part 148 (done): partition-level disk management (ADR-0158, task #844)

`disk_enumerate()` now reports partitions as ordinary entries (`is_partition`/`parent_disk`), not just whole disks -- `diskrole.c`/`diskformat.c` needed zero code changes of their own, since both already key every operation purely off `disk_enumerate()`'s own name/dev_path/is_os_disk fields. A new `diskpart.c` adds synchronous, `sfdisk`-scripted primitives (partition-table creation is metadata-only and near-instantaneous, unlike `format`'s async mkfs).

#### Added
- `POST /v1/disks/{name}/partition-table` -- destructive: writes a fresh, empty GPT table to a non-OS whole disk with no role or partitions of its own currently in use. Same `confirm_disk_name` double-confirmation as `POST .../format`.
- `POST /v1/disks/{name}/partitions` -- appends one new partition via `sfdisk --append` (never touches an existing one); `size_mib` omitted/0 means "rest of the disk," the same convention the installer's own fixed-layout `auto_partition()` already established.
- `DELETE /v1/disks/{name}/partitions/{partition_name}` -- removes one partition; `409` if it still has a role assigned or is mounted.
- `cixctl disks partition-table|add-partition|rm-partition` + matching web-adjacent CLI docs.

#### Fixed
- `DISK_ENUM_MAX` raised `64` -> `256` -- a real, previously-undiscovered silent-truncation gap found live while testing this task: a dev sandbox whose `/sys/class/block` is shared with its own LXC host sees every one of the host's own unrelated LVM `dm-*` volumes (72 of them here) in the same enumeration, and `readdir()` order doesn't guarantee a real target disk's own entries come first, so the old cap could silently drop a real disk (or here, all of its partitions) with no error. Not new to this task -- whole-disk enumeration already shared the same array -- but partitions sharing the same budget made it easier to hit.

#### Verified
- Real, against a spawned `cixd`: `GET /v1/disks` correctly reports `is_partition`/`parent_disk`/empty-model/removable:false for this sandbox's own real, pre-existing partitions, with parent linkage verified against the same list. Every validation-only rejection path (invalid name, not found, wrong resource kind, wrong parent, missing field, wrong confirm) exercised as real HTTP requests. A disk (and separately a partition) with a role assigned directly to it correctly rejects the destructive operation with 409 -- safe to test for real since role assignment is pure daemon-side bookkeeping.
- NOT verified: the real `sfdisk`-invoking success path end to end through the daemon -- this sandbox has no loop devices and no safe, disposable real block device. The exact sfdisk script syntax was instead confirmed by hand against a scratch disk image file (sfdisk operates identically on a plain file as a real block device). See ADR-0158's own Verification section for the full disclosure.

### Part 147 (done): parallel package builds -- design only (ADR-0157, task #841)

A complete, actionable design for task #841 (configurable concurrent package builds, default 10) -- deliberately not implemented in the same session it was designed. `pkg.c`'s "one job at a time" turns out to be woven into at least ten module-level statics, a hardcoded single build-container name, and a single-purpose reactor conn kind -- real, substantial surgery on the single most heavily-used subsystem in the project, not something to rush at the tail end of a long session, per this project's own "Outline -- Execute -- Verify" workflow.

#### Design
- Build-transient fields (overlay paths, output capture, cache-hit flag) move onto the already-existing per-package `pkg_entry` table rather than a new parallel array.
- One small new table, sized to the concurrency limit (not the full package table), tracks in-flight dependency chains -- the one piece of state that's genuinely per-request rather than per-package.
- **A real simplification found while designing**: the shared, cumulative `g_pkgbuild_rootfs` merge-back looked like it would need new locking under real concurrency, but doesn't -- this daemon has no real threads, and every event handler already runs to completion before the next one starts, so two completions can never actually interleave regardless of how many builds are running concurrently off in their own child processes. No new synchronization primitive needed, only correct per-entry state (already covered above).
- A phased implementation plan (pure-refactor phase first, verifiable against the existing test suite with zero behavior change, before any real concurrency is enabled) for whoever picks this up next.

### Part 146 (done): live network attach/detach on a running container, closes task #861 (ADR-0156)

The "network" piece of task #861 (`cmd`/files/network updates without a recreate) -- files already shipped as ADR-0153. `cmd` is closed by explanation rather than code: killing a container's init process to change what it runs necessarily destroys its own PID namespace (`pid_namespaces(7)`, a real kernel invariant), so there is no way to swap a container's command without an architecturally-real recreate. Network is different and genuinely tractable -- network namespaces have no such "dies with init" rule.

#### Added
- `POST /v1/containers/{name}/networks` -- attaches a network to an already-running container live: a real veth pair, moved into the running container's own netns via `setns()`, renamed/addressed/brought up from inside it. Same request shape as one entry of `POST /containers`' own `"networks"` array.
- `DELETE /v1/containers/{name}/networks/{network}` -- the reverse. Deleting either end of a veth pair removes both, so no `setns()` is needed for this direction. Only ever removes a *live* attachment (409 for a create-time one -- tearing that down mid-life would silently diverge a running container from its own persisted definition).
- `cixctl container network attach|detach`.
- `registry_network_attachment` gained `veth_host`/`ifname` -- `ifname` is now populated for every attachment, create-time included (previously computable from array position but never stored; a live attachment's real kernel-side name can outlive its own array index after an earlier detach shifts the array, so deriving it from index would have been actively wrong once this shipped).
- Deliberately live and ephemeral, the identical posture ADR-0153 already established: never touches the container's own persisted body. A restart/recreate replays the original definition, any live attachment gone. The durable path is a container recipe (ADR-0151).

#### Verified
- Full clean rebuild (`-Wall -Werror`), zero warnings. New coverage in `test/test_daemon_net.c`: a container started with zero networks (its own listener already bound to a wildcard address before any interface exists) gets one live-attached, a real TCP connection through the new interface succeeds, `GET` reflects it as `"live":true`, it's detached, `GET` shows it gone, then re-attached again with another real successful connection (proving no veth-naming collision across a full cycle). Error paths (nonexistent network/container, double-attach, detach-never-attached, detach-a-create-time-attachment) all covered. Full regression sweep (`test_daemon`, `test_cli`, `test_web`, `test_container_net`, `test_networks`, `test_network_interfaces`, `test_container_lifecycle`, `test_routes`) clean afterward.
- A real test-authoring mistake was caught before shipping: the first draft of the create-time-detach-rejected check reused a container from an earlier scenario in the same file, whose own listener had already self-exited after consuming its fixed connection quota -- silently testing the wrong (404, "not running") path instead of the intended 409. Fixed with a dedicated container built specifically for that assertion.

### Part 145 (done): task #865 closed for real -- the first real self-hosted cixd deploy to 192.168.15.95, and the real bugs it took to get there

The actual deploy of ADR-0150's PTY fix to the real box turned out to require closing three genuine, previously-undiscovered bugs in mechanisms that had shipped code-complete but never been exercised end to end for real. Documented here as one arc since they were found and fixed in direct sequence chasing the same deploy.

#### Fixed
- **ADR-0154**: `mkbootroot`'s server-side `mksquashfs` invocation now sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for a `cix-hosttools`-sourced binary -- without it, the dynamic linker silently linked against whatever `liblzma.so.5` the bare host already had instead of the one actually built for it.
- **squashfs-tools 4.7.5-5**: the real bug behind "`mksquashfs` reports success but produces a byte-swapped, invalid squashfs" -- confirmed via a direct, isolated test (running the built binary inside a real container from its own image, bypassing `mkbootroot` entirely) that the output's own magic bytes read `sqsh`, the exact reversal of the real `hsqs`. Root cause: TCC never predefines the bare `linux` macro GCC always does on a Linux target (confirmed via a trivial local `#ifdef linux` probe), and squashfs-tools' own `endian_compat.h` branches its entire byte-order detection on exactly that macro. Fixed with `-Dlinux=1`, steering TCC onto the same, correct `<endian.h>`-based branch GCC's own predefined macro would already select -- not a source patch, supplying the one macro a real GCC build already has.
- **ADR-0155** (documented, not a code fix): `pkg_seed_image_baseline()`'s own "self-heals on its very next install" doesn't survive a same-manifest reinstall -- ADR-0108's image-version hash is a manifest hash, so reinstalling an already-present package at its own unchanged version dedupes straight back to the pre-existing (still-missing-the-fix) directory. Confirmed live, twice (`psmisc`, then `screen`), before finding the real unblock: installing a package the image genuinely didn't have yet (`xz`, `recipes/image/jumpbox/1.3.0`) forces a real fresh build.
- `recipes/package/cix/v1.54.0`: re-pinned (task #852) carrying the LD_LIBRARY_PATH fix -- the first tag that could actually deploy.

#### Verified
- Full self-hosted build+deploy cycle against the real box, start to finish: built `cix-builder` (tcc/make/libc-dev/bash/coreutils/openssl) and `cix-hosttools` (coreutils/gzip/openssl/zlib/curl/tar/bzip2/xz/squashfs-tools) images live, ran `pkg hostbuild cix --deploy`, confirmed a real, `hsqs`-valid squashfs staged to the inactive slot, rebooted, confirmed the box came back on the new slot with all 7 containers auto-started.
- jumpbox1's own live `/dev/ptmx` confirmed present post-fix via a direct `exec("/dev/ptmx")` probe (`EACCES`, not `ENOENT`) on its exact running image version; `follow_rolling:true` correctly picked up the new version automatically, no manual recreate.
- A full, real SSH connection to jumpbox1 (`ssh -tt`) confirmed the handshake and host-key exchange succeed cleanly, failing only at the authentication step (no LDAP credential available from this session to complete a full authenticated PTY request) -- the root cause (missing devpts mount / missing `/dev/ptmx`) is independently confirmed closed by the direct probe above.
- `e2fsprogs 1.47.4-2`'s own `PROG_SUBDIRS=misc` fix (a real, separate TCC linking gap in `e2fsck`, unrelated to the ones above) is documented as still real but explicitly out of scope for tonight -- `mke2fs` (the only binary this project actually uses) was never affected.

#### Scope
- Test containers/images created during this investigation (`squashtest`, `ptytest`–`ptytest6`, `ptmxtest`) all cleaned up afterward, real box left in a clean, verified-working state.

### Part 144 (done): root-cause investigation of a real cixd hang on 192.168.15.95, swap enabled as mitigation (task #875)

Real, live incident: after a burst of legitimate work (several image-recipe applies, multiple `pkg install` calls) `cixd` on 192.168.15.95 stopped responding to HTTP entirely -- TCP `accept()` still succeeded instantly, but no request ever completed, for an extended period. No SSH/console access existed to investigate live; the box was eventually recovered by an out-of-band reboot (a real, hard-to-avoid loss of the in-memory forensic state -- the previous boot's kernel ring buffer and any further live diagnosis went with it).

#### Investigated
- The `audit`-source log (every mutating request) shows the daemon's very last logged action was a `POST /v1/pkg/install` that reached its install-completion step (a non-fatal `tar`/`gzip` cache-save failure -- the same pre-existing, already-documented, deliberately-non-fatal gap from earlier in this session) -- then total silence, no further requests logged at all. The step that runs immediately after the cache-save inside that same synchronous completion path, `merge_tree()` (a plain recursive `opendir`/`readdir`/`lstat`/copy over local disk, no timeout anywhere in the chain), is the most likely place a single slow or stuck filesystem operation would block the daemon's entire single-threaded event loop -- exactly matching the observed symptom (`accept()` succeeds, nothing after it ever runs).
- Three containers (`jumpbox1`, `dns-1`, `dns-2`) show `exited (status=9)` log lines inside the same time window -- initially looked like a crash, but cross-referencing the `audit` log showed each one immediately preceded by a real `DELETE`+`POST /v1/containers` pair from this session's own earlier, deliberate recreate work, not an anomaly. Ruled out as a red herring before it was reported as a finding.
- The box has only 8GB RAM and swap was disabled (`{"enabled":false}`) -- a real, plausible amplifier already anticipated by this project's own swap feature (ADR-0069, raised originally for "a package build ran a box out of RAM"): under memory pressure with no swap to absorb a spike, a stalled single-threaded process reads from the outside exactly like what was observed.

#### Honest scope, stated explicitly
- **Not proven with certainty.** No `oom-killer` kernel log line survived to confirm memory pressure directly, and the box has since been rebooted, foreclosing further live investigation of this specific instance. This is the best-supported hypothesis given the available evidence (last logged action, the specific unbounded operation that runs next, and the absent swap safety net), not a confirmed root cause.
- The deeper structural fix -- bounding or moving long host-side filesystem/subprocess operations in the pkg install-completion path off the single event-loop thread, so one slow operation can never block all HTTP serving -- is real follow-on work that overlaps directly with task #841's already-planned parallel-package-builds redesign (which needs to touch this exact code path anyway), not attempted as a rushed, disconnected patch here.

#### Mitigated
- 8GB host swap enabled on 192.168.15.95 (`POST /v1/system/swap`, done via the web dashboard's Host > Swap page) -- confirmed live via `GET /v1/system/stats` (`swap_total_bytes: 8589930496`). Directly addresses the most likely amplifying factor regardless of whether the exact trigger above is fully correct.

Auditing `recipes/image/jumpbox/1.1.0/build.sh` directly against the real box's own `pkg ls --image=jumpbox` output found a real drift: `procps` (`ps`/`top`/`free`/`kill`/etc., an existing recipe since Phase 31) was installed live onto the real box's jumpbox image during this same session (task #835) to fix a real "psmisc has pstree, not ps" gap the user hit directly -- but was never added to the git-tracked image recipe itself. The same class of bug task #837 already closed once for a different set of recipes: the recipe, not the live box, is what a fresh or rebuilt jumpbox actually gets built from, so a live-only addition is invisible to every future deployment.

#### Fixed
- `recipes/image/jumpbox/1.2.0/build.sh` (new version, recipe versions are immutable once published): adds `procps:rolling:4.0.6` to `image_packages`. No new transitive dependency -- `procps.recipe` declares no `pkg_depends`.

#### Verified
- `test_pkg_sync`/`test_image_recipe` clean. With this fix, the jumpbox tooling audit (task #842) is now genuinely complete: every tool installed live on the real box's jumpbox image is also present in the git-tracked recipe that would rebuild it.

### Part 142 (done): validate + document image-version pinning for running containers (task #874)

User-reported, after installing `procps` onto the real box's jumpbox image and finding the already-running `jumpbox1` container still had no `ps`: "when we adjust an image, it's not picking things up? Or a container? the cool thing about our approach is that we package manage containers on the fly, right?" Investigated and confirmed the answer is **no, by deliberate design** (ADR-0107/0108/0124, already implemented and already covered by `test/test_rolling_restart.c`, re-run clean here as live confirmation) -- every install against an image produces a new, immutable, content-addressed rootfs version, never a mutation in place; a container pins the specific version it was created against and keeps running against that exact directory forever. The only previously-undiscovered gap was that this well-established mechanism had no plain-language, operator-facing explanation anywhere outside the ADRs and a dense `api/README.md` paragraph.

#### Added
- `docs/guides/administration.md`: new "Does installing a package onto an image reach containers already running from it?" section -- the direct answer, plus the two real ways to actually get new content onto a running container (recreate, or opt into `follow_rolling: true`), and a pointer to ADR-0153's live single-file `PUT .../files` for the unrelated "quick config patch" case.
- `recipes/container/README.md`: a real worked example container recipe (`echo-web`), closing a genuine dangling link -- `recipes/README.md` has linked to `recipes/container/` since ADR-0151 (Part 137), but the directory had never actually held any committed content (git doesn't track empty directories), so the link 404'd. Found via a repo-wide, script-based markdown link/anchor resolution sweep (177 files, 0 broken afterward) run as part of this task's own verification.

#### Scope
- Purely additive documentation plus one pre-existing dangling-link fix -- no code changes; the underlying mechanism (ADR-0107/0108/0124) was already fully implemented and tested before this task.

### Part 141 (done): live, single-file container updates without a recreate (ADR-0153, task #861)

`PUT /v1/containers/{name}/files?path=...` writes or overwrites one file inside an already-existing container -- running (via `/proc/<pid>/root`, overlay copy-up lands it in the real upperdir) or stopped/exited (direct to upperdir) -- without recreating the container. Deliberately live and ephemeral: never touches the container's own persisted `files[]` body, so a future restart/recreate replays the original definition unchanged. The durable "survive a recreate" path stays a container recipe (ADR-0151).

#### Added
- `PUT /v1/containers/{name}/files?path=...` (`daemon/src/main.c`'s `handle_container_file_write()`), same `{content, mode, owner, group}` shape as a `files[]` entry.
- `cixctl files put NAME --path=/some/path --file=LOCAL_PATH [--mode=0644]`.
- New permanent test coverage in `test/test_container_files.c`: a full write/read round-trip against a *running* container (proving the `/proc/<pid>/root` + overlay-copy-up path, checked directly against the real host-visible `upper/` file's content/mode/owner/group, not just a 204), an overwrite-replaces-not-appends check, the same traversal/no-leading-slash/missing-content/unknown-container rejections the read side already has, and a write/read round-trip against an already-exited container (the `!running` branch).

#### Fixed
- A real use-after-free caught during this feature's own verification, before it shipped: the first implementation read `content` as a pointer straight out of the parsed JSON tree, then called `json_free(root)` *before* using that same pointer in the subsequent `write()` -- a real end-to-end test wrote 17 bytes and read back 17 bytes of garbage instead of the actual content. Fixed by taking an owned `strdup()` copy before freeing the JSON tree, freed explicitly on every return path.

#### Scope, stated explicitly
- `cmd`, network attachment, and other non-file option updates without a recreate remain unimplemented -- task #861 stays open for that remaining scope; this part closes the files-only piece of it.

### Part 140 (done): audit every recipe for the ambient-gcc-contamination risk (task #845)

CLAUDE.md's own environment notes already documented a real, confirmed bug class: this session's `openssh/10.4p1-7`/`-8` recipes needed an explicit `CC=tcc` after the shared build sandbox's own bare `cc` silently started resolving to real GCC instead of TCC (`gcc.recipe`'s own toolchain output merging into the cumulative sandbox). Audited every one of the 78 package recipes for the same exposure.

#### Fixed
- 68 recipes had a real, confirmed `./configure` or plain `make` invocation with no explicit compiler pin -- every one now sets `CC=tcc` (or, for `perl.recipe`, Perl's own documented `-Dcc=tcc` `Configure` flag, since its bespoke `Configure` script doesn't reliably honor a bare environment `CC=` under `-des`).
- A real mistake caught during this same pass, not shipped: the first automated sweep also added `CC=tcc` to `tcc.recipe` itself, which its own header comment explicitly documents as deliberately built with the shared sandbox's **real gcc** (bootstrapping) -- reverted before committing. `gcc.recipe`'s own `CC=tcc` (bootstrapping gcc *from* tcc) is correct and was kept; `kernel.recipe`/`openssl.recipe`/`gitea.recipe`/`cix.recipe` were confirmed, by their own existing header comments, to already be deliberate real-gcc exceptions and were left untouched.

#### Scope, stated explicitly, not left an unstated gap
- **Not rebuild-verified.** No bootstrapped local toolchain sandbox was available during this audit (the real box, 192.168.15.95, was unreachable at the time -- see the same session's cixd-hang incident), so none of these 68 recipes were actually rebuilt end to end after the change. Each edit is a minimal, mechanical, additive compiler pin matching the exact pattern already proven correct for `openssh`/`sysklogd` -- low-risk, but genuinely unverified by a real build, and flagged as such rather than assumed safe.

New `test/test_hostauth.c` coverage: real `expires_in_seconds` shown, no raw token anywhere in the response, revoking a user immediately invalidates its existing token, revoking a user with no session is a real no-op (204). Full regression sweep clean. User-requested directly: "let's make the container recipes so it will make things easier in the future." ### Part 133 (done): every container gets a real devpts mount + /dev/ptmx (ADR-0150, task #865)

User-reported, real: an interactive `ssh osakka@192.168.15.109` (jumpbox1) failed with `PTY allocation request failed on channel 0` -- every prior test only ever used non-interactive `ssh ... id`, never exercising real pty allocation. Root cause, confirmed by reading the code: `pkg_seed_image_baseline()` never seeded a `/dev/ptmx` node (only `null`/`zero`/`full`/`random`/`urandom`), and `mountns_pivot()` never mounted `devpts` inside a container's own mount namespace -- the identical bug class task #764 already fixed once for the daemon's own host-namespace console-exec feature, one namespace layer deeper, never addressed for containers themselves.

#### Added
- `src/mountns.c`'s `mountns_pivot()`: a fresh `devpts` mount at `/dev/pts` on every container start (`mode=0620,ptmxmode=0666`, identical options to the host's own `boot_init()` mount), same "fresh every start" treatment as `/proc`/`/sys`/`/run`.
- `daemon/src/pkg.c`'s `pkg_seed_image_baseline()`: a `/dev/ptmx` symlink to `pts/ptmx`, seeded alongside the five existing static device nodes -- self-heals into every pre-existing image automatically, since this function re-runs on every install, not just an image's first version.
- New permanent regression test, `test/test_container_pty.c` + `test/pty_child.c`: a real container allocates a pty exactly the way `sshd`'s own interactive session does (`posix_openpt`/`grantpt`/`unlockpt`/`ptsname_r`/open the slave/round-trip a byte).

#### Fixed
- A real regression caught by the new test's own first run, before it ever left this session: the first version of the `mountns_pivot()` change assumed `/dev` already existed, which broke `test_overlay.c`/`test_container_net.c`'s own minimal hand-built lowerdirs (no `/dev` at all) outright. Fixed by giving `/dev` itself the same guaranteed-present treatment as `/proc`/`/sys`/`/run`.

#### Verified

### Part 132 (done): unified `recipes/package/` + `recipes/image/` git layout (ADR-0149)

Follow-up to task #867 (commit the 4 already-built image recipes to git, wire `pkg sync` to walk them, closing the gap ADR-0123 flagged): mid-implementation, the user pointed out `pkg/recipes/` (versioned) and the new `pkg/image-recipes/` (flat, name-only) didn't read as one coherent system. Full regression sweep clean.

### Part 131 (done): glauth's own baseDN becomes daemon-managed (ADR-0148)

Direct follow-up to Part 130: the user asked whether the LDAP base DN should be "genuinely dynamic" rather than fixed by hand. Investigated directly: it lived in four independently-authored places (`hostauth-config.ldap_base_dn`, each registered server's own `glauth.cfg [backend] baseDN`, and each *client* container's own `nslcd.conf`/`ldap-authkeys.conf`), agreeing only because the same string had been typed into all four this session.

#### Added
- `hostauth_ldap_base_dn()` (`daemon/src/hostauth.c`): the real getter for what's now genuinely the one canonical source of truth.
- `rewrite_basedn()` (`daemon/src/ldap.c`): finds a `baseDN = "..."` line (glauth's own real, confirmed double-quoted TOML convention) within a registered server's preserved config prefix and rewrites just that value to match `hostauth_ldap_base_dn()`, on every write `ldap_write_config_file()` already does (registration, every user/group mutation). No match (single-quoted, or absent) is a legitimate no-op -- never invents structure. An empty (never-configured) `ldap_base_dn` skips the rewrite rather than blanking out a working value.

#### Fixed
- Two pre-existing doc inaccuracies, found while auditing this exact area, both predating this change: `docs/api/openapi.yaml`/`docs/api/README.md` both claimed LDAP server registration "never touches the container's filesystem" -- false since task #726 (registration has always immediately pushed the current user/group set). Only "never sends a signal" was ever accurate.

#### Scope, stated explicitly, not left an unexplained gap
- Client-side files (`nslcd.conf`, `ldap-authkeys.conf`, anything else staged into an arbitrary container's own `files[]`) stay deliberately, permanently manual -- Cix has no model of those containers to safely template into, and inventing one would be exactly the kind of unintuitive magic this change was asked to avoid, not fix.

#### Verified
- Full clean rebuild, zero warnings. New `test/test_ldap.c` coverage: a registered server's own real `baseDN = "dc=old,dc=example"` line survives untouched while `ldap_base_dn` is still unset, then gets correctly rewritten (new value present, old gone, every other prefix line -- `datastore`, `IgnoreCapabilities` -- intact) once `ldap_base_dn` is set and any LDAP mutation triggers the next sync. 3 consecutive clean runs, full daemon-linked regression sweep.

### Part 130 (done): renaming an LDAP user or group in place (ADR-0147)

User-requested, following the live-infrastructure re-provisioning: `PUT /v1/ldap/users|groups/{name}` previously discarded the request body's own `name` field outright (`(void)body_name; /* the URL path's name is authoritative for PUT, not the body's own */`) -- the only way to rename a record was delete-then-recreate.

#### Added
- `PUT /v1/ldap/groups/{name}` and `PUT /v1/ldap/users/{name}`: a real, different `name` in the body now renames the record (omitted or identical: no rename, unchanged behavior). Validated the same way `POST .../create` validates a new name.
- **Real, deliberate cascade on the group side only**: `daemon/src/hostauth.c`'s new `hostauth_rename_admin_group()` -- if the group's old name is currently a member of `hostauth-config`'s own `admin_groups` list, it's rewritten to the new name and persisted, called from `ldap_group_update()` after the group's own rename is durably saved but before the request is considered successful. A renamed admin group can never silently drop out of write-gating -- the same class of incident ADR-0146 closed once already, a different cause this time.
- `cixctl ldap group update --name=NAME --gidnumber=N [--new-name=NEWNAME]`, `cixctl ldap user update --name=NAME [--new-name=NEWNAME] ...` -- a distinct flag from `--name=` (which keeps meaning "which record"), not a reused one.

#### Fixed
- A pre-existing gap in `ldap_user_update()`, found while adding rename's own revert-on-persist-failure path: no field was ever rolled back in memory on a `save_users_state()` failure (only the newly-added name-revert is; the rest of that gap is unchanged, out of scope for this change).

#### Verified
- Full clean rebuild (`-Wall -Werror`, zero warnings). `test/test_ldap.c`: rename mechanics for both users and groups (old name gone, new name resolves, collision rejected). `test/test_hostauth.c`: the critical safety property -- renaming the *currently active* admin group, confirming `admin_groups` follows automatically, and that a fresh login still succeeds immediately after. 3 consecutive clean runs of both, plus the full daemon-linked regression sweep.

#### Infrastructure stood up (live state, no code changes)
- `dns-1`/`dns-2` (192.168.15.101/.102, `dnsmasq`), registered as DNS servers, host resolver repointed at both. Real recursive resolution confirmed (`dig @dns-1 example.com`).
- `ldap-1`/`ldap-2` (192.168.15.103/.104, `glauth` 2.4.0 -- rebuilt from source this session, see below), registered as LDAP servers. `hostauth-config` switched to `ldap_enabled: true`; verified end to end including across a real reboot (the exact ADR-0146 regression scenario) -- login, write-gating, and the rendered config all survived intact.

- `jumpbox1` (192.168.15.109, `openssh`+`linux-pam`+`nss-pam-ldapd`+`bash`+`coreutils`), real live-LDAP SSH login confirmed both ways: password (`pam_ldap.so`'s bind-as-user check) and pubkey (`AuthorizedKeysCommand`'s live `ldapsearch`), wrong password correctly rejected.

#### Real bugs found and fixed along the way
- **glauth's `config` backend needs an explicit `sshkeyattr = "sshPublicKey"`** in `[backend]` -- confirmed via its own source (`pkg/handler/config.go`): with no default assignment, an unset `SSHKeyAttr` renders the pubkey attribute with an empty name. Baked into the standard `glauth.cfg` template used for both servers.
- **`nslcd.conf` needs `pam_authc_ppolicy no`** -- glauth's `config` backend doesn't handle the LDAP password-policy control `nslcd` requests by default, and answers a real, otherwise-correct bind with a spurious `Invalid credentials` instead of ignoring the unsupported control.
- **A real, standard OpenSSH privsep interaction, closed properly, not worked around**: with `UsePAM yes`, PAM's own conversation (and therefore `pam_ldap.so`'s conversation with `nslcd` over its local socket) runs inside `sshd`'s own privsep pre-auth child, which `chroot()`s to `--with-privsep-path` before that conversation happens -- confirmed directly via `/proc/mounts` inside a real running container (`/run` is its own tmpfs; `/` is the overlay root, a different filesystem than `-7`'s `/var/empty`), so a hard link of `/run/nslcd/socket` into the chroot failed with `EXDEV`. Fixed with a new recipe version, `openssh/10.4p1-8/build.sh` (`--with-privsep-path=/run/sshd-empty` instead of `/var/empty`, everything else unchanged from `-7`), putting the chroot target on the same filesystem the socket already lives on so the same-device hard link actually works. `jumpbox1`'s own startup script hard-links the socket in after `nslcd` has bound it, before starting `sshd`.
- **`nss-pam-ldapd`-authenticated `sshd` needs a real, minimal `/etc/passwd`/`/etc/group`** even for accounts it never logs in as -- `--with-privsep-user=sshd` means `sshd`'s own privsep child needs a real local `sshd` account to exist (this project's minimal images have none by default), and `AuthorizedKeysCommandUser` needs a real local account too (`authkeys`, uid/gid 75, matching the convention Part 123 already established for the file-rendered predecessor's own credentials file).
- `pkg/recipes/cix/v1.4.0/build.sh` re-pinned to `v1.49.0` (task #852) and `glauth/2.4.0/build.sh`'s dead `pkg_source` URL re-served, both real, separate gaps found and fixed while standing this infrastructure back up -- see the dedicated commit for full detail (`pkg_sha256`/access token in the `cix` recipe are left as explicit placeholders, never a committed secret, matching that recipe's own established convention -- publishing it live still needs a real token this session has no credential for).

#### Verified
- Full clean rebuild (`-Wall -Werror`, zero warnings) of the `openssh` `-8` revision. Live, real, end-to-end SSH sessions against `jumpbox1` for both password and pubkey auth, wrong password correctly rejected, confirmed via the real container's own captured `sshd`/`nslcd` logs and `glauth`'s own server-side bind log, not just client-side exit codes.

Applied live to 192.168.15.95 first (`PUT /v1/system/daemon-config {"port":80,"https_port":443}`, confirmed both new ports answering and 7620 gone), then made the actual default so a *fresh* install starts here too.

#### Changed
- `daemon/src/main.c`: `DEFAULT_PORT` 7620 -> 80.
- `daemon/src/daemon_config.c`: `DEFAULT_HTTPS_PORT` 8443 -> 443.
- `cli/src/main.c`: `DEFAULT_PORT` 7620 -> 80, matching (a `cixctl` with no `--port=` now reaches a freshly-started `cixd` with no `--port=` by default, same as before this change just at the new numbers).
